creator: David Blair
results.description: This flier by David Blair advertises JustArt, an exhibition of artists' posters he helped organise to raise money for a campaign to stop the New Zealand Rugby Union's proposed tour of South Africa in 1985. The exhibition was held in Auckland and supported by the National Council of Churches. About twenty artists were involved, many connected to Artists Against Apartheid (which had become Auckland Artists Action by this time).The attempt to tour South Africa was only four years after the bruising experience of the Springbok rugby tour to New Zealand in 1981. Many New Zealanders had objected to that tour because of South Africa's policy of racial apartheid. Protests had caused obstruction and the cancellation of games, and much violence between protesters, supporters and police.The posters were activist in intent but were made for collection and display, rather than for pasting up on city walls. David Blair screenprinted posters for about fifteen of the artists in his studio (the other artists had their own studios). The exhibition was a success, raising about NZ$6000 (personal communication with artist, 2022).Renewed protest activity in 1985 demonstrated that the same issues remained. The proposed tour was cancelled as a result of a successful legal challenge.

creator: David Blair
results.description: This poster by David Blair was his contribution to JustArt, an exhibition of artists' posters he helped organise to raise money for a campaign to stop the New Zealand Rugby Union's proposed tour of South Africa in 1985. It features black and white figures uniting as they rise above the heat of conflict.The exhibition was held in Auckland and supported by the National Council of Churches. About twenty artists were involved, many connected to Artists Against Apartheid (which had become Auckland Artists Action by this time).The attempt to tour South Africa was only four years after the bruising experience of the Springbok rugby tour to New Zealand in 1981. Many New Zealanders had objected to that tour because of South Africa's policy of racial apartheid. Protests had caused obstruction and the cancellation of games, and much violence between protesters, supporters and police.The posters were activist in intent but were made for collection and display, rather than for pasting up on city walls. David Blair screenprinted posters for about fifteen of the artists in his studio (the other artists had their own studios). The exhibition was a success, raising about NZ$6000 (personal communication with artist, 2022).Renewed protest activity in 1985 demonstrated that the same issues remained. The proposed tour was cancelled as a result of a successful legal challenge.
